scientific_checks.basis: All eight critical r0 losses have unknown references; remaining all_of conjuncts are true and any_of reserve routes false, so neither false nor true dominance masks the critical loss.
Both restoration polarities supply eligible r0 and decisively produce ready/not_ready; negative restoration is a new adverse value rather than a physical reversal of the original passing evidence.
all_of retains false r0 and makes r1 unknown, compared with negative-restored position 8; any_of retains a true primary route and makes reserve r2 unknown, compared with positive-restored position 6.

One case-level rule fixes operators, thresholds, age windows, scope keys and routes. Fact scope/status/date manipulations deliver missing/stale/invalidated/wrong-version conditions; admission rules are not changed to manufacture answer keys.

Six adversarial fixture patterns per logic family cover simultaneous stale/inactive/wrong-version blockers, retaining blocked history during positive/negative restoration, future/wrong-version records and inclusive age-five versus age-six boundaries. These are calibration fixtures outside the recipient denominator.

Final scripted wire review checks 120 exact inputs and clone states, 40 three-reasoner position groups, common donor files/observations across positions, actual first request equality and computed EAL/conventional conclusions against the independent raw-fact evaluator.

Prompt packets omit expected_decisions, authored answers, condition/cause metadata, manipulation labels and comparator labels; donor notes are absent. Public expected_value fields are criterion bounds. Asset names contain cause labels identically across reasoners, so they remain a shared cue and cause-domain confounding limit.

Primary is communicated verdict correctness plus internal explanatory consistency; canonical enum correctness is separate. Masked coders receive answer text only. Factual explanation accuracy/grounding remains unassessed. Ambiguity and no explanation cannot establish primary success.
